crop.notes: Whole item, headline 'A Fighter on His Muscle.' to the end; the clipping is split into two stacked pieces in one image.

ocr.notes: Mostly right but with meaning errors: the image says Allen knocked out Egan (not Brooks), Egan 'once kept' the Canterbury (not 'owned'), the dog was a 'quiet spectator', and Tom 'shook himself away' from the men. Headline missing from transcript.

title.suggested: Allen knocks out Jim Egan in a fight at his free-and-easy

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch reported that Tom Allen knocked out Jim Egan, once keeper of the Canterbury, in a quarrel at Allen's free-and-easy, then drew a pistol on Egan's dog but put it away and had the men ejected.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'St. Louis Post-Dispatch Monday, October 29, 1883', page 2; item near bottom of the fifth column.

facts.fact: A short time before Oct. 29, 1883, a couple of thugs attacked Allen and tried to rob him, believing he was past his prime

Allen knocked out Jim Egan, who once kept the Canterbury, in a quarrel at Allen's free-and-easy; Egan's friend Brooks and Egan's dog joined in, Allen drew his pistol on the dog but put it away, and Egan and his friends were ejected

notes: The current title says 'trouble maker'; the item names Jim Egan and Brooks. The brawl happened 'a couple of days ago', i.e. about Oct. 27, 1883.
